html:
The Sihasapa, or Blackfoot Lakota, are one of the seven bands of the Lakota, the western branch of the Sioux. The name means "black feet". They are a different people from the Algonquian Blackfoot of Montana and Alberta.

The map places them in what is now northwest South Dakota, but in 1492 the Lakota still lived further east, around the upper Mississippi. They moved west onto the plains in the 1700s, after they got guns and the horse. There they hunted bison and lived in tipis, alongside the other Lakota bands such as the Hunkpapa and the Itazipco.

In the wars with the United States in the 1860s and 1870s, many Sihasapa fought beside Sitting Bull. Their descendants live mainly on the Standing Rock and Cheyenne River reservations.
